hero.title: Stand-ins & picture doubles
hero.lede: Accurate matches to your leads, experienced on set — so lighting holds, cameras keep turning and your actors' hours go where they matter.

difference.heading: Six jobs, often confused. Here's what each one does.

cards.title: Stand-in
cards.body: Takes the actor's place while shots are lit and blocked. Matched on height, build and colouring so every setup translates exactly when the actor steps in. Rarely on camera.

cards.title: Picture double
cards.body: Appears on camera in place of the actor — over-the-shoulder angles, hands, driving shots and distance work. The match has to hold in the frame, not just under the lights.

cards.title: Body double
cards.body: Steps in for specific physical work — physique shots, movement, anything the schedule or the script keeps the actor from doing. Cast to match in close quarters.

cards.title: Intimacy double
cards.body: Performs intimate scenes in the actor's place, working to the intimacy coordinator's choreography — cast with consent, closed-set experience and a match that holds in frame.

cards.title: Hand double
cards.body: Close-up insert work — writing, driving, product handling, instruments. Matched on skin tone, size and detail, steady under a macro lens.

cards.title: Stunt double
cards.body: Takes the action the actor can't — falls, fights, vehicle work — under the stunt coordinator, matched closely enough to cut seamlessly with the performance.

whyItMatters.heading: A good match keeps the whole unit moving.

rows.label: LIGHTING & CAMERA
rows.text: Setups are lit and blocked on a true match — nothing shifts when the actor steps onto their mark.

rows.label: A MOVING SET
rows.text: Your leads rest, rehearse or shoot on another unit while setups continue without them.

rows.label: SCHEDULE & COST
rows.text: Fewer resets and less actor downtime — the saving compounds across every shoot day.

matching.heading: Matched to your leads, not close enough.
matching.note: Send your leads' details or casting references — we shortlist from measured, photographed artists on our books, not self-reported stats.

rows.label: CAMPAIGN SHOOTS
rows.text: Lighting doubles for principal talent on limited hours — setups ready the moment they arrive.

rows.label: STILLS & CONTENT
rows.text: Hands, product interaction and distance work shot on a double while your talent covers the hero frames.

rows.label: TIGHT SCHEDULES
rows.text: One shoot day instead of two — a match on set is often the cheapest hour a smaller production can buy.

cards.title: Set-ready people
cards.body: Experienced stand-ins who know set etiquette — where to be, when to be silent, how to hold a mark and take direction from the camera department.

cards.title: Admin handled
cards.body: Contracts, fees, overtime and on-the-day coordination dealt with by us — one invoice, no chasing.

cards.title: One relationship
cards.body: Doubles, dancers, fighters and specialists through a single point of contact — one roster, every format.
